notes: Eleven labelled turns, no stenographer notes, no headings. The page opens WITH a label ('Sr. Torres. –' on the first text line), so it does not open mid-utterance. After the chair's 'Se lo computo.' an unlabelled indented paragraph follows ('Para una interrupción, tiene la palabra la señora senadora Negre de Alonso.'); by rule 2 that is a run-on paragraph of the same chair turn, not a new turn. Label terminator throughout is an en dash preceded by a period; the period is set bold in some labels ('Sr. Torres. –') and roman in others ('Sr. Torres. –' on the third line, 'Sra. Escudero. –'), the office/holder split is bold 'Sr. Presidente' + roman '(Pampuro)'. I recorded every label in the same normalised spelling 'Name. –' because the difference is one of weight, not of characters. The chair label carries a surname here (Pampuro) even though this is a pre-2016 page. Typographic oddity: 'Sr. Presidente (Pampuro). –  La senadora...' has a double space after the dash, and inside Torres's long speech there is a double space after '¿cómo se le va a enseñar a un chico estas cosas?  Entonces'. No footer is printed on this page.
